q: FortiAnalyzer supports two operation modes. Name them and describe the primary role of each. How does log storage differ in Collector mode versus Analyzer mode?
kp: Analyzer mode: receives, analyzes, stores (SQL database), and reports on logs
Collector mode: primary task is forwarding logs of connected devices to an Analyzer and archiving them
In Collector mode logs are retained in their original binary format for uploading instead of being written to the database
In Collector mode most features are disabled

q: According to the Analyzer/Collector feature comparison, which FortiAnalyzer features are available in BOTH modes, which are Analyzer-only, and how does Log View differ between the two modes?
kp: Available in both: Device Manager, System Settings, Log Forwarding
Analyzer-only: FortiView, Incidents & Events, Reporting, monitoring devices
Log View: full in Analyzer mode; raw archive logs only in Collector mode

q: In FortiAnalyzer HA, what rule must be followed regarding Initial Sync during initial cluster setup, what happens if all nodes violate it, and how is the Failover Threshold related to the Heart Beat Interval (give the default values)?
kp: During initial setup, at least one node must have Initial Sync disabled
The primary node is elected from among the nodes with Initial Sync disabled
If all nodes have Initial Sync enabled during initial setup, the cluster gets stuck trying to synchronize
Failover Threshold = Heart Beat Interval x 3 (defaults: Heart Beat Interval 4 seconds, Failover Threshold 12 seconds)

q: Which HA operation modes does FortiAnalyzer support, and what is the purpose of the Cluster Virtual IP including its connectivity requirement?
kp: Active-Passive or Active-Active operation modes
Active-Active is used to create a geo-redundant solution
Cluster VIP is optional
Cluster VIP requires a layer 2 connection between HA members (if no VIP, select the peer communication interface as Heart Beat Interface)

q: Which TCP port does FortiAnalyzer use for HA traffic, which port do FortiGate and FortiManager use for OFTP to FortiAnalyzer, and which port does FortiManager use for managing FortiAnalyzer?
kp: HA: TCP/5199
OFTP from FortiGate and FortiManager: TCP/514
FortiManager management of FortiAnalyzer: TCP/541

q: What is a FortiAnalyzer dataset, how are charts related to datasets, and can predefined and custom datasets be cloned?
kp: A dataset is a collection of log messages from monitored devices
Charts in FortiAnalyzer are generated based on datasets
You can use predefined datasets or create custom datasets by querying the log messages in the SQL database
Both predefined and custom datasets can be cloned

q: What is a FortiAnalyzer Fabric, how do its members exchange information, and what type of deployment is it ideal for?
kp: FortiAnalyzer Fabric enables centralized viewing of devices, incidents, and events across multiple FortiAnalyzer members
One device operates in supervisor mode as the root device
Incident, event, and log information is synced from members to the supervisor using the API
Ideal for high volume environments with many FortiAnalyzers

q: What is Analyzer-Collector collaboration in FortiAnalyzer, and why would you deploy it?
kp: Deploy Analyzer mode and Collector mode on different FortiAnalyzer units working together
Improves overall performance of log receiving, analysis, and reporting
The Analyzer offloads the log receiving task to the Collector
This maximizes the Collector's log receiving performance while the Analyzer focuses on analysis and reports

q: In FortiAnalyzer HA, what is the default role of a new cluster unit, when can a secondary unit become primary, and what does the Log Data Sync option do?
kp: Default role is Secondary so the unit can synchronize with the primary unit
A secondary unit cannot become a primary unit until it is synchronized with the current primary unit
Log Data Sync is on by default and provides real-time log synchronization among HA units

q: Which TCP ports does FortiAnalyzer expose for its JSON API (HTTPS and HTTP) and for its Web Service (SOAP/XML API)?
kp: JSON API: TCP/443 (HTTPS) and TCP/80 (HTTP)
Web Service (SOAP/XML API): TCP/8080
